title: Find Polygon With the Largest Perimeter
summary: Given an array of positive integers nums, find the largest possible perimeter of a polygon that can be formed using the elements of nums as side lengths.
statement: Given an array of positive integers nums, find the largest possible perimeter of a polygon that can be formed using the elements of nums as side lengths. If it is not possible to form any polygon, return -1. A polygon can be formed if the sum of the lengths of any (k-1) sides is greater than the length of the kth side, where k is the number of sides.
constraints: nums contains at least three positive side lengths.
A chosen set forms a polygon exactly when its longest side is strictly less than the sum of the others.
Return the largest obtainable perimeter, or -1 if no subset forms a polygon.
hints: After sorting, the prefix before a side is the greatest possible sum of smaller available sides.
Scan in ascending order with a prefix sum; whenever prefix exceeds the current side, record their total.
Maintain prefix; if prefix>value set answer=prefix+value, then include value in prefix.
Adding positive sorted sides only increases perimeter, so the latest valid prefix is optimal; a failed side cannot help without later accumulated sides.
editorial: Adding positive sorted sides only increases perimeter, so the latest valid prefix is optimal; a failed side cannot help without later accumulated sides.

tests.explanation: All three sides form a triangle with perimeter fifteen.
Sides 1,1,2,3,5 form the largest valid polygon, with perimeter twelve.
